_comment: Which prose document describes which part of the code, and the commit each
was last read against it. scripts/doc_reconciliation.mjs turns that into the
question 'which documents are OWED a reading', which is the half of doc rot
that is mechanical. Whether a document is TRUE is not mechanical and this
file does not pretend otherwise -- see the header of the script.
Adding a document here is cheap and is the right response to finding a stale
claim in one. 'subjects' are the paths whose movement should send somebody

README.md.why: test counts, the tool and role tables, Known Limits, and the [chain] section all describe code that moves

docs/GUIDE.md.why: the adoption guide: every command, error message, default and recipe it quotes was run against this commit; agents follow it verbatim

docs/POSITIONING.md.why: claims about what has and has not been measured; it said no Terminal-Bench score was claimed while three campaigns sat in the repository

docs/EVIDENCE.md.why: one row per claim; a benchmark that runs and is not added here is a result that went missing from the summary

docs/CONTRACTS.md.why: the exit codes, the enumerations, the record shapes and the TOML subset

docs/ROADMAP.md.why: phase checkboxes describing what is built; P2 claimed an extension host that nothing calls

docs/HARNESS-RESEARCH-RECONCILIATION.md.why: asserted 'TaskRecord carries no stop_reason' for days after it gained one -- the case that motivated this file

docs/BENCHMARKS.md.why: describes the suites and what each is worth

docs/EXTERNAL-BENCHMARKS.md.why: maps gnomon's records and control properties onto three external benchmarks; the mapping rots when the audit record or the tool set changes
